items.headline: Credit investors still won't believe the AI-debt rally has ended
items.summary: CoreWeave's five-year CDS spread topped 1,140bps and its bonds yield near 15% even as equities staged a recovery Oct 19; Oracle's CDS widened to a record ~288-315bps as the investment-grade AI bellwether. Evercore ISI said credit markets are pricing AI debt without operating-cash-flow support.
items.actionable: Treat renewed CoreWeave/Oracle CDS widening as an early warning to keep the cash pile intact and avoid AI-capex-adjacent credit risk; it's also a tailwind for GDX/SILJ as a safe-haven hedge if contagion resumes.

items.headline: China Q3 GDP beats at 4.5%, but investment and retail sales stay weak
items.summary: China's NBS reported Q3 2026 GDP growth of 4.5% y/y (vs 4.4% expected, up from 4.3% in Q2), with September exports up 36.3% and industrial output up 5.5%. Retail sales grew just 1.1% and fixed-asset/property investment fell, underscoring weak domestic demand.
items.actionable: The export-led beat is modestly supportive for Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC and China-exposed SGX names (Yanlord, CapLand China Trust), but soft retail sales and falling investment argue against chasing the China-consumption leg of the book.

items.headline: Fed enters blackout ahead of Oct 27-28 FOMC; hold now the consensus
items.summary: The Fed's communications blackout runs Oct 17-29 through the Oct 27-28 meeting. Hike odds on prediction markets fell back to roughly 14-15% (from ~70% a month ago) after an initial post-CPI spike, with a hold priced at ~84-87% and a December cut still seen as unlikely.
items.actionable: With a hold now consensus, near-term tail risk for rate-sensitive SGX banks and REITs (DBS/OCBC/UOB, Mapletree, Keppel REIT) is lower into month-end; hold dry powder for entries after the Oct 28 decision rather than chasing pre-meeting moves.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export pause nears Nov 10 expiry with no extension yet published
items.summary: Beijing's one-year pause on its October 2025 rare-earth export controls lapses November 10, 2026, and as of October 16 no extension notice had appeared on the commerce ministry's list, even though Washington claims a truce running to January 10, 2027. The pause never covered the separate April 2025 licensing regime for heavy rare earths like dysprosium and terbium.
items.actionable: The unresolved Nov 10 deadline is the single biggest near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels watchlist -- continued Beijing silence into early November should be read as bullish for Western rare-earth supply-chain names.

items.headline: Brent falls over 2% toward $107-109 on Russia sanctions waiver even as Hormuz flows stay depressed
items.summary: Brent crude fell more than 2% Monday after Trump waived certain Russia sanctions/tariffs, easing supply fears, while WTI dropped near $98-100. The seven-day moving average of Hormuz oil flows remains at just 8.5 million bpd versus a normal ~20 million bpd, keeping a geopolitical floor under prices.
items.actionable: Easing Brent on the Russia waiver, despite Hormuz flows still roughly 60% below normal, reinforces precious metals over energy as the preferred macro hedge in the book right now.

items.headline: GCC urges US-Iran talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz as Iran's 7-day plan stays 'on the table'
items.summary: Iran's FM Araghchi said Tehran's proposed seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz remains viable, with the strait reopening on day six if Washington agrees and negotiations starting day seven. The GCC publicly called for resumed US-Iran talks to restore freedom of navigation, while Qatar and Pakistan continue mediating.
items.actionable: A credible path to reopening Hormuz is a potential bearish catalyst for crude and could also deflate part of the geopolitical risk premium currently supporting gold/silver -- watch for an air-pocket in both if talks progress.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds $80-83k band despite AI-equity deleveraging
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $81,000-$83,000 on Oct 19, briefly testing the $80,750-$81,000 support zone over the weekend before reclaiming $81,300-$81,500 on rising volume. QCP Capital flagged that ongoing equity deleveraging tied to AI-credit stress could still test the $80k level.
items.actionable: BTC's resilience in the $80-83k band is a tentative risk-on signal; a clean break below $80k would likely coincide with further de-risking pressure on HK tech and AI-adjacent names elsewhere in the book.

items.headline: Singapore banks hit by mark-to-market losses after Citi downgrade sparks selloff
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB extended declines into this week, with OCBC down roughly 10% and DBS down about 6% over a two-session stretch following Citi's 'sell' downgrade on softer Q3 earnings expectations earlier in October. OCBC reports Q3 results on November 6, 2026.
items.actionable: Avoid adding to SG bank exposure ahead of the Nov 6 OCBC print; reassess bank weighting only after Q3 results clarify whether the mark-to-market losses are earnings-relevant or technical.

items.headline: Lynas agrees ~A$968m Meteoric Resources acquisition for Brazilian heavy rare earths
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths agreed to acquire Meteoric Resources, gaining the Caldeira ionic-clay heavy rare earths project in Brazil, in a deal that would lift Lynas's measured-and-indicated TREO resources by 79% and reserves by 26% pro forma. It follows Lynas becoming the first non-China supplier of dysprosium and terbium, with FY2026 revenue up 76% y/y to AUD 977.95 million.
items.actionable: The Meteoric deal reinforces the long-term rare-earth watchlist thesis and argues for keeping Lynas near the top of that basket given its first-mover heavy-rare-earth position.

items.headline: JPMorgan upgrades Yangzijiang Shipbuilding to Buy after fresh $920m order win
items.summary: JPMorgan raised Yangzijiang Shipbuilding to Buy with a SGD 6.70 target on Oct 16, 2026, days after the company announced roughly US$920 million in new orders that sent shares up about 6.5%. The orderbook stands at 258 vessels with large-vessel delivery slots booked through 1H30.
items.actionable: The upgrade plus order momentum supports holding/adding to the existing YZJ position into the November 4 earnings print.

items.headline: Silver/SLV whipsaws as institutions buy SILJ dip while Reddit sentiment turns bearish
items.summary: SLV fell 6% in a session through a key technical level (SILJ -5.9%) before rebounding with SLV +3.39% and GDX +4.34% on Oct 15; meanwhile institutional buyers including Vontobel Holding (new $7.03M SILJ position) and Veracity Capital (+45.2% stake) added to junior-silver-miner holdings in Q3 2026 even as Reddit sentiment on SLV sank from 50.49 to 40.59.
items.actionable: The split between institutional accumulation and souring retail sentiment is a classic contrarian setup -- don't get shaken out of SILJ/SLVP/GDX positions on short-term technical breaks.

items.headline: US softens chip-enforcement posture on China ahead of Trump's Beijing visit, even as CXMT wobbles
items.summary: Reports indicate the Commerce Department is recalibrating its 2025 technology offensive, downplaying new restrictions and approving higher-tier chip exports to China ahead of a planned Trump visit to Beijing, even as enforcement actions targeting SMIC dealings (e.g. the Exyte fine) continue. Separately, Chinese memory maker CXMT's shares fell 7.8% on Oct 19 despite record nine-month profit.
items.actionable: A softer US enforcement posture ahead of the Beijing visit is incrementally supportive for SMIC's addressable market even as peer CXMT wobbles on margins -- watch for read-through at SMIC's next earnings update.

items.headline: CapitaLand China Trust shores up balance sheet with Yuhuating mall sale ahead of Q3 print
items.summary: CapitaLand China Trust signed an agreement to sell CapitaMall Yuhuating at an RMB 748 million floor price, retaining a 5% strategic stake, with proceeds earmarked for debt repayment, unit buybacks or working capital. CLCT reports Q3 2026 results on October 23, 2026.
items.actionable: The Yuhuating disposal modestly de-risks CLCT's balance sheet ahead of the Oct 23 print -- reassess the China-retail-REIT leg of the SGX book once results confirm whether same-store DPU trends are holding.
